added.comedō: The card’s verb (Comēde, comēderis) with its Lewis & Short link s.v. comedo; the dictionary form, with the long final ō the lexicon writes everywhere, is the term of the record (eat up) that carries these examples.
added.sūcus citreī: Nominative of the card’s own sūcum citreī (Vīsne sūcum citreī in pisce?), as the term of the record that carries that example; both words occur in the cards.

flags: entry-298: “Comēde tōtum piscem!” has a long ē; comedō has a short e in the present stem (Lewis & Short cŏm-ĕdo, ēdi), so the imperative is comede, as entry-411 writes (“comede ea”). comēderis (future perfect) is right.

entry-268 cremum vs entry-298 crēmum: one word, two quantities, both cited to Traupman 71. Traupman p. 71 prints cremum; his English–Latin vocabulary (p. 298) prints crēmum. The record leads with cremum (the libellī’s cremō fartī); 298 also calls crēmum post-classical, kept as its period.

entry-251: jūsculum “sauce, broth (Traupman 73)”. Traupman 73 gives iūs for sauce and iūs, iūsculum for soup (p. 70 broth); Lewis & Short has jūsculum only as “a broth” (Cato). The sauce record may want jūs.

entry-407 jam: the note copies the card, “L&S has conditūra, from condō, preserve”. But Lewis & Short has two words: conditūra (condō) “a preparing, making” (Petr. 51.5), and condītūra (condiō) “a preserving of fruits” (Col. 12.48.1), which supports Traupman’s condītūra.
entry-416 loaf tin: the card prints artopta, artoptae f.; Lewis & Short has artopta, ae, m. (both the baker and the bread-pan).

entry-257 apron: the card cites M-O for praecīnctōrium, but M-O s.v. apron recommends gremiāle and līmus (Verg.; Isid.) and says praecīnctōrium in the passages they saw means a loin-covering (Adam and Eve’s fig leaves); Lewis & Short cites only Aug. Genes. c. Manich. 2.2.
entry-407 sweets: Lewis & Short also has the feminine plural cuppēdiae, “dainty dishes” (late: Gell. 7.13.2; Amm.), so Traupman’s cuppēdiae is attested late; the note keeps the card’s wording.
entry-415: the card’s heading prints “māchina mīxtōria”, against its own item and the mixtus ruling (mixtōria).
entry-415 says “the lexicon follows caffēa”, but ōlla caffeae (272) and māchina/mola caffeāria (415) have a short e.

Departures from a printed source that the cards do not explain, so no note was added: crustulum (Traupman 71 crūstulum), līmōnāta (Traupman 71 līmonāta), fūsōrium (Traupman 125 fusōrium; Lewis & Short fūsōrium), vāsculum (Traupman 323 vasculum), coquīnātōria (Traupman 124 coquinātōria), crāstinum (Lewis & Short crastĭnus; Bennett’s long a), ēscāria (Lewis & Short escārius; the series’ ēsca).

Likely overlaps with other batches (records created anyway): be-hungry (entry-80, hungry); eat-up and drink-beverage (entry-84, eat/drink; entry-116 has pōtiō); dessert (entry-250); freezer (entry-127); bottle (entry-248); chop-finely and dice (entry-123); kitchen-utensils (entry-128, īnstrūmenta culīnāria); salt-cod (entry-207, natura); lemon-juice (entry-114 lemon, entry-116 juice); eat-out (entry-228, urbs); jug-of-water (entry-119, jug); napkin’s mantēle is the domus hand towel (entry-64). The existing colander record lists “sieve” in also; sieve is now its own record (crībrum).

Recommended forms chosen where the card did not settle it: napkin leads with mappa (what Libellus IV uses) over the card’s first-listed mantēle (the house hand towel); pancake leads with laganum (the card’s examples) over artolaganus; dishes leads with vāsa (entry-259) and keeps entry-413’s vāsa ēscāria as an alternative; cooking-pot keeps caccabus, with ōlla, “the series spelling” in entry-251, added as an alternative.

Periods set from Lewis & Short where the card cites only a modern source: pānis autopȳrus (Petr. 66.2), vāsa coquīnāria (Plin. 33.140), vāsa ēscāria (Plin. 36.198), pullus gallīnāceus (Plaut. Capt. 4.2.69; the card cites M-O after Vives), ōvum hapalum (Scribonius Largus, besides Apicius), fūsōrium (post-classical: Pall. 1.17.1), corpus facere (cf. Phaedr. 3.7, fēcistī tantum corporis). Modern for Traupman’s pāniculus “roll” (classically a tuft: Lewis & Short s.v. pānicula). minūtim concīdere is left modern (M-O) though it may well be classical.
